<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="440.7mm" height="469.9mm" viewBox="0 0 440.7 469.9" data-device="ex4550-32t" data-view="bottom" data-weight-note="19.4 lb (8.8 kg) with one power supply (Table 6)" data-depth-note="18.50 in (46.99 cm) (Table 6)" data-rj45-speeds="10 GbE, 1 GbE or 100 Mbps on each fixed port" data-expansion-ports="up to 48 ports with two 8-port modules, or 2 x 40 GbE with a QSFP+ module" data-power-max-w="403" data-power-envelope="fully-configured" data-power-input-ac="100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 7.8 A and 3.8 A" data-power-input-dc="operating range -36 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 7 A maximum" data-redundancy-note="two supplies, load sharing; do not mix AC and DC, or AFI and AFO" data-fans="three fan modules and a fan in each supply; the switch runs 30 seconds while one fan module is replaced" data-heat-btu-h="1375 BTU an hour at the maximum system power (Table 22)" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F)" data-humidity="10 to 85 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no loss of performance to 10,000 ft (3,048 m)" data-software="Junos OS, first release 12.2R4" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches, mixed with EX4200 and EX4500; a 10GBASE-T port joins only EX4550 switches" data-expansion="two module slots (front and rear), EX4550-EM-8XSFP, EX4550-EM-8XT, EX4550-EM-2QSFP and EX4550-VC-128G" data-oob="one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps" data-console="mini-USB console port (active) and RJ-45 console port (passive)" data-usb="one USB port" data-seismic="GR-63, Issue 4, Zone 4 (guide Table 28)" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://www.nomios.com/news-blog/juniper-announces-end-of-life-of-popular-ex-switches/" data-end-of-sale="2019-06-30" data-end-of-life="2024-06-30" data-airflow="back-to-front" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.

       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */

      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }

    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }

    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }

    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }

    g[data-ref^='juniper/ex4600-jpsu-650-ac-afo@'] .state-amber { --led-color: #f5a623; }
    g[data-ref^='juniper/ex4600-jpsu-650-ac-afo@'] .state-green { --led-color: #39b54a; }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="440.7mm" height="469.9mm" viewBox="0 0 440.7 469.9" data-device="ex4550-32t" data-view="bottom" data-weight-note="19.4 lb (8.8 kg) with one power supply (Table 6)" data-depth-note="18.50 in (46.99 cm) (Table 6)" data-rj45-speeds="10 GbE, 1 GbE or 100 Mbps on each fixed port" data-expansion-ports="up to 48 ports with two 8-port modules, or 2 x 40 GbE with a QSFP+ module" data-power-max-w="403" data-power-envelope="fully-configured" data-power-input-ac="100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 7.8 A and 3.8 A" data-power-input-dc="operating range -36 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 7 A maximum" data-redundancy-note="two supplies, load sharing; do not mix AC and DC, or AFI and AFO" data-fans="three fan modules and a fan in each supply; the switch runs 30 seconds while one fan module is replaced" data-heat-btu-h="1375 BTU an hour at the maximum system power (Table 22)" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F)" data-humidity="10 to 85 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no loss of performance to 10,000 ft (3,048 m)" data-software="Junos OS, first release 12.2R4" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches, mixed with EX4200 and EX4500; a 10GBASE-T port joins only EX4550 switches" data-expansion="two module slots (front and rear), EX4550-EM-8XSFP, EX4550-EM-8XT, EX4550-EM-2QSFP and EX4550-VC-128G" data-oob="one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps" data-console="mini-USB console port (active) and RJ-45 console port (passive)" data-usb="one USB port" data-seismic="GR-63, Issue 4, Zone 4 (guide Table 28)" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://www.nomios.com/news-blog/juniper-announces-end-of-life-of-popular-ex-switches/" data-end-of-sale="2019-06-30" data-end-of-life="2024-06-30" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {

    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>

<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="469.9mm" height="43.7mm" viewBox="0 0 469.9 43.7" data-device="ex4550-32t" data-view="right" data-weight-note="19.4 lb (8.8 kg) with one power supply (Table 6)" data-depth-note="18.50 in (46.99 cm) (Table 6)" data-rj45-speeds="10 GbE, 1 GbE or 100 Mbps on each fixed port" data-expansion-ports="up to 48 ports with two 8-port modules, or 2 x 40 GbE with a QSFP+ module" data-power-max-w="403" data-power-envelope="fully-configured" data-power-input-ac="100 to 120 VAC and 200 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 7.8 A and 3.8 A" data-power-input-dc="operating range -36 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 VDC, 7 A maximum" data-redundancy-note="two supplies, load sharing; do not mix AC and DC, or AFI and AFO" data-fans="three fan modules and a fan in each supply; the switch runs 30 seconds while one fan module is replaced" data-heat-btu-h="1375 BTU an hour at the maximum system power (Table 22)" data-operating-temp="0 to 40 C (32 to 104 F)" data-humidity="10 to 85 percent noncondensing" data-altitude="no loss of performance to 10,000 ft (3,048 m)" data-software="Junos OS, first release 12.2R4" data-virtual-chassis="up to 10 switches, mixed with EX4200 and EX4500; a 10GBASE-T port joins only EX4550 switches" data-expansion="two module slots (front and rear), EX4550-EM-8XSFP, EX4550-EM-8XT, EX4550-EM-2QSFP and EX4550-VC-128G" data-oob="one RJ-45 management port with link and status lamps" data-console="mini-USB console port (active) and RJ-45 console port (passive)" data-usb="one USB port" data-seismic="GR-63, Issue 4, Zone 4 (guide Table 28)" data-eol="announced" data-eol-announcement="https://www.nomios.com/news-blog/juniper-announces-end-of-life-of-popular-ex-switches/" data-end-of-sale="2019-06-30" data-end-of-life="2024-06-30" data-airflow="front-to-back" data-power="ac">
  <style>
    [data-path] { cursor: pointer; }
    .state-on    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-up    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    /* link and up are the same fact on an Ethernet lamp; see docs/rj45-family-design.md */
    .state-link  { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-activity { --led-color: #86efac; }
    .state-ok    { --led-color: #22c55e; }
    .state-fault { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-fail  { --led-color: #ef4444; }
    .state-locate { --led-color: #3b82f6; }
    .state-absent { opacity: 0.35; }
    /* A SWITCHED OUTLET WITH NO LAMP is dimmed when it is off, as absent is but
       less (docs/pdu-model-design.md section 3.2): every switched PDU in the
       library has a lamp per outlet, and this is the fallback so the first one
       without does not invent a lamp. An outlet a lamp is bound to by `for:`
       carries data-lamped (mark_lamped) and is never dimmed: its lamp says it. */
    [data-class='inlet'][data-states~='off'].state-off:not([data-lamped]) { opacity: 0.55; }
    /* A state is a colour AND a behaviour. Solid and blinking of the same colour
       are different facts on real hardware: on the S9510-28DC a solid green PWR
       is "system power good" and a blinking green PWR is "power good but BMC
       power fail". A blinking state that renders solid is the same failure as a
       state class nothing paints - it looks modelled and is not.
       blink animates opacity rather than fill, because each skin carries its own
       unlit colour in the fill fallback and a keyframe cannot name it. alternate
       animates fill, because two colours is the whole point, and takes its first
       value from the element's own fill. */
    @keyframes portrayal-blink {
      0%, 49.9% { opacity: 1; }
      50%, 100% { opacity: 0; }
    }
    @keyframes portrayal-alternate {
      0%, 49.9% { fill: var(--led-color, #3a3f44); }
      50%, 100% { fill: var(--led-color-alt, #3a3f44); }
    }
    .portrayal-highlight { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.2px #f59e0b) drop-shadow(0 0 0.5px #f59e0b); }
    .portrayal-dim { opacity: 0.25; }
    [data-class='region'].portrayal-highlight { stroke: #f59e0b; stroke-width: 0.7; filter: none; }
    .state-fail[data-class='psu'], .state-fail[data-class='fan'] { filter: drop-shadow(0 0 1.4px #ef4444); }
</style>
